title: Event delta reconciler for console usage with checkpointed idempotent hydrator
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: build a resilient 'delta reconciler' service that can apply compacted usage deltas to the canonical analytics view while guaranteeing idempotency and resumability. This is intended for cases where source telemetry (eventstream) had gaps, duplicates, or schema drift and we need to replay corrected derivations without corrupting downstream aggregates or double-counting tokens/costs.

Why this ticket exists: existing ad-hoc backfills are manual, error-prone, and take large windows offline. We need a production-grade operator that: (1) consumes delta streams (compact, typed change records) from Kafka, (2) applies them to the OLAP staging area and the canonical usage store with per-entity idempotency, (3) writes robust checkpoints to S3 for resume, and (4) emits reconciliation metrics and per-run manifests for audit.

Non-goals: full reingestion of raw blobs, real-time serving changes, or replacing existing one-off analytic backfills during migration windows. This is targeted at mid-window replays (hours->days) and small historical corrections (days->weeks).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Reconciler can consume a compacted delta topic and apply changes to canonical usage storage without producing duplicate totals for the same entity when the same delta is replayed.
2) Resume from S3 checkpoint and continue processing from the last committed offset with exactly-once semantics for applied deltas.
3) Exposes per-run manifests (run id, input offsets, applied counts, error buckets) to the console UI and infra logs.
4) Integration tests that inject duplicated and out-of-order deltas demonstrate idempotent application and produce expected post-reconcile aggregates within tolerance.
5) Runbook and rollback steps documented in Confluence and linked in the ticket.
implementation_plan: Design delta record schema and idempotency token: schema doc + sample payloads in Confluence
Prototype consumer: lightweight go/kafka consumer that materializes deltas to staging tables with idempotency checks
Checkpointing layer: S3 manifest format and atomic commit protocol (write-to-temp->rename) + retention policy
Apply worker: transactional applier that uses optimistic checks and conflict markers for multi-part updates
Observability: metrics (applied, dropped, errors), run manifests, stackdriver logs and console dashboard hooks
Integration tests: simulated double-send/out-of-order deltas and CI pipeline that validates aggregates
Canary backfill: run on a small customer set and validate differences with historical baseline
Ops docs and runbook: recovery, forced-replay, and safe-abort procedures
notes: Decision: use compacted Kafka topic per logical entity to make delta consumption window-bounded and reduce storage pressure.
Trade-off: exactly-once across the full pipeline is expensive; we implement idempotent appliers + checkpointed offsets to achieve practical exactly-once for applied deltas.
Safety: every apply writes an audit row into a dedicated "applied_deltas" table with run_id + idempotency_token to allow easy verification and rollback.
Performance constraint: apply worker must sustain peak velocity of 5000 deltas/sec in worst-case backfill windows—benchmark target included in runtime-1.18 perf doc.
Security note: manifests include checksums and signer metadata; secrets used for KMS will be rotated per infra security policy. Security review is required before broad rollout.

2025-02-18 Miguel Ortega: PoC consumer implemented (go) and validated against synthetic delta generator. Found edge-case with out-of-order keys when compaction lag > 15m; added reordering buffer to design.
2025-02-22 Priya Raman (Data Eng): Reviewed checkpoint format; suggested using atomic rename to avoid partial-manifest visibility. Also requested retention policy for manifests (90 days default).
2025-02-27 Security Team (Sophie Li): Flagged KMS integration and recommended threat model doc for manifests containing PII (we'll partition manifests to exclude PII and store only checksums).

2025-03-03 QA (Evan Brooks): Integration tests added. Simulated duplicate-delivery scenario passed, but found a race when two appliers target the same aggregate concurrently—implementing per-aggregate optimistic lock and retry in next PR.
2025-03-04 Miguel Ortega: WIP - implementing optimistic lock and adding canary run tooling. Planning canary for 2025-03-10 on internal sandbox cluster.
